info.description:
NOT SERVED AT PRESENT. This document is the contract of an API that is published for reading and not yet switched on: every request to https://ronutz.com/api/* answers HTTP 404 with {"error":"api_not_served"}. The in-browser tools at https://ronutz.com/en/tools/ compute every result below, locally.

The programmatic counterpart to the in-browser tools at ronutz.com.

Every operation here is a pure function: the same input always yields the
same output, nothing is stored, and no request bodies or query values are
logged. The browser tools remain the zero-egress default for sensitive work;
this API exists for automation (scripts, pipelines, integrations).

The surface grows with the toolbox: every shipped tool is exposed here and
documented from the same registry, so the served endpoints and this document
cannot drift apart. Only shipped tools are listed (no vaporware). Each
operation accepts its input via GET (?input=) or POST (the request body) and
returns a JSON result.

Operations whose request and response are written out field by field carry
examples whose requests come from the tool's golden vectors; the build re-runs
every one of them through the engine and fails if a documented value differs.
Every operation carries `x-golden-vector-set`, the id of the golden-vector set
its contract was last checked against.

get.description:
Two modes, chosen by `mode`. Without it (or with `"timers"`), the request gives both systems' Desired Min TX
Interval, Required Min RX Interval and Detect Mult, optionally their Required Min Echo RX Interval and Demand
mode, plus the session state (`sessionUp`, default true) and the path (`single-hop`, the default, or
`multihop`). The answer gives, for each direction (A to B, then B to A), the agreed transmit interval, the
larger of the sender's Desired Min TX and the receiver's Required Min RX (RFC 5880 sections 6.8.2 and 6.8.7); the
jitter range (0 to 25% shorter, 10 to 25% when the sender's Detect Mult is 1, section 6.8.7); the packet rate;
the detection time the receiver computes (the sender's Detect Mult times the agreed interval in Asynchronous
mode; in Demand mode the receiver's own Detect Mult times its own agreed transmit interval, section 6.8.4);
RFC 7419 Common Interval membership; and whether Echo packets may flow (section 6.8.9, never over multiple
hops, RFC 5883 section 3). While the session is not Up every Desired Min TX is raised to 1 s (section 6.8.3).
Every number comes with explanations, each carrying the section it comes from.

Intervals are strings with a unit (`us`, `µs`, `ms` or `s`, such as `"300ms"`) or integers in microseconds.
Warnings name a Required Min RX of 0 and any value below a floor that a downloaded vendor document states
(FRRouting bfdd: 10 ms; Junos OS 13.1, 2013: 1 ms).

With `"mode": "decode"`, `packet` is a BFD Control packet in hex (24 to 255 bytes; spaces, colons, hyphens,
dots and a leading 0x allowed); the answer reads every field of RFC 5880 section 4.1, names the first receive
check of section 6.8.6 that discards the packet (`discardedBy`, or null), and lists other findings.
Authentication data is never echoed back: only Auth Type and Auth Len.

parameters.description: The request object as a URL-encoded JSON string.

200.description: The two directions of the session, or the decoded packet.

frrExample.summary: FRRouting's detect-multiplier example, 900 ms at the remote system (golden vector frr-detect-multiplier-example)

explanations.text: A may not send Control packets to B faster than the larger of its own Desired Min TX (300 ms) and B's Required Min RX (200 ms): 300 ms. A, the slower side, sets the rate.
A shortens each interval by a random 0 to 25% to avoid self-synchronisation, so its packets leave every 225 ms to 300 ms, about 262.5 ms on average (roughly 12.5% less than the agreed interval).

explanations.section: computed: 1 s divided by the agreed interval
explanations.text: At 300 ms the rate before jitter is 3.333 per second, a little higher after it.

B declares the session Down, with diagnostic 1 (Control Detection Time Expired), after 900 ms without a valid packet from A: A's Detect Mult (3), which B receives in every packet, times the agreed interval (300 ms). Roughly, 3 packets in a row must be lost.
300 ms is not in RFC 7419's Common Interval set. A hardware implementation that cannot run it adjusts towards a larger interval; the next Common Interval is 1 s.
B advertises a Required Min Echo RX of 0: it will not loop Echo packets back, so A sends none.
B may not send Control packets to A faster than the larger of its own Desired Min TX (300 ms) and A's Required Min RX (300 ms): 300 ms. Both ask for the same interval.
B shortens each interval by a random 0 to 25% to avoid self-synchronisation, so its packets leave every 225 ms to 300 ms, about 262.5 ms on average (roughly 12.5% less than the agreed interval).

explanations.section: computed: 1 s divided by the agreed interval
explanations.text: At 300 ms the rate before jitter is 3.333 per second, a little higher after it.

A declares the session Down, with diagnostic 1 (Control Detection Time Expired), after 900 ms without a valid packet from B: B's Detect Mult (3), which A receives in every packet, times the agreed interval (300 ms). Roughly, 3 packets in a row must be lost.
300 ms is not in RFC 7419's Common Interval set. A hardware implementation that cannot run it adjusts towards a larger interval; the next Common Interval is 1 s.
A advertises a Required Min Echo RX of 0: it will not loop Echo packets back, so B sends none.

notes.text: Single-hop Control packets use UDP destination port 3784 (Echo packets 3785) and, without authentication, a TTL or Hop Limit of 255.

upPacket.summary: An Up packet at 300 ms, bytes computed from RFC 5880 section 4.1 (golden vector up-300ms)

findings.text: Diagnostic 0: No Diagnostic, the sender's reason for the last change in its session state.
State Up: the session is established, as the sender sees it.
Control Plane Independent (C) is clear: the sender's BFD shares fate with its control plane.
Required Min Echo RX Interval is zero: the sender will not loop Echo packets back.

get.summary: CGN port blocks and MAP port sets (RFC 7768, RFC 7422, RFC 7597)
get.description:
One JSON object in, naming its mode; the same engine as the page at /tools/cgn-port-blocks.

`blocks` (RFC 7768 section 2, RFC 6888 REQ-2 and REQ-4): `pool` (a prefix, a range, one address, or a count of
addresses), `portRange` (default `1024-65535`, above the System Ports of RFC 6335), `blockSize`,
`blocksPerSubscriber` (default 1), and optionally `subscribers` or `inside` (a prefix counted as its host
addresses, or a range), and `logFormat` (`nat444`, 150-byte messages, or `ds-lite`, 175 bytes, RFC 7422 section
1). A subscriber's blocks are counted on one address (paired pooling). The log figures use RFC 7422's 33,000
connections per day and divide by the block size, RFC 7768's reduction factor: computed, not measured.

`deterministic` (RFC 7422 section 2, algorithm 0, Sequential): `inside` (I), `outside` (O), and optionally
`reserved` (R, default `0-1023`), `compressionRatio` (C, default I / O rounded up), `dynamicFactor` (D, default
0), `maxPorts` (M), `lookup` (an inside address), `reverse` ({`address`, `port`, `time`}), `configFrom`,
`configUntil` and `recordTime` (UTC, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`). Each inside address gets floor(candidates / (C +
D)) ports, in order; the rest is the dynamic pool. With more than one outside address, the outside addresses are
filled in order, C inside addresses each. `configRecord` is the section 3 record when I and O are prefixes and M
is given. The table is returned for up to 256 inside addresses.

`map` (RFC 7597 section 5.1 and Appendix B, used unchanged by MAP-T, RFC 7599): `offset` (a), `psidLength` (k),
and a `psid` (a number, or a string in decimal or `0x` hexadecimal) and/or a `port`. Returns the port set's
ranges (up to 1,024 listed) and, for a port, the PSID that owns it, or `excluded` when its A field is 0.

One JSON object in, naming its mode; the same engine as the page at /tools/cgn-port-blocks.

`blocks` (RFC 7768 section 2, RFC 6888 REQ-2 and REQ-4): `pool` (a prefix, a range, one address, or a count of
addresses), `portRange` (default `1024-65535`, above the System Ports of RFC 6335), `blockSize`,
`blocksPerSubscriber` (default 1), and optionally `subscribers` or `inside` (a prefix counted as its host
addresses, or a range), and `logFormat` (`nat444`, 150-byte messages, or `ds-lite`, 175 bytes, RFC 7422 section
1). A subscriber's blocks are counted on one address (paired pooling). The log figures use RFC 7422's 33,000
connections per day and divide by the block size, RFC 7768's reduction factor: computed, not measured.

`deterministic` (RFC 7422 section 2, algorithm 0, Sequential): `inside` (I), `outside` (O), and optionally
`reserved` (R, default `0-1023`), `compressionRatio` (C, default I / O rounded up), `dynamicFactor` (D, default
0), `maxPorts` (M), `lookup` (an inside address), `reverse` ({`address`, `port`, `time`}), `configFrom`,
`configUntil` and `recordTime` (UTC, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`). Each inside address gets floor(candidates / (C +
D)) ports, in order; the rest is the dynamic pool. With more than one outside address, the outside addresses are
filled in order, C inside addresses each. `configRecord` is the section 3 record when I and O are prefixes and M
is given. The table is returned for up to 256 inside addresses.

`map` (RFC 7597 section 5.1 and Appendix B, used unchanged by MAP-T, RFC 7599): `offset` (a), `psidLength` (k),
and a `psid` (a number, or a string in decimal or `0x` hexadecimal) and/or a `port`. Returns the port set's
ranges (up to 1,024 listed) and, for a port, the PSID that owns it, or `excluded` when its A field is 0.

get.summary: IPv4 CIDR calculator (subnet, special-purpose classification, VLSM, supernet, overlap / gap)
get.description:
The four modes of the CIDR / Subnet Calculator, from the same engine the page runs.

Subnet (the default): a bare block such as `192.168.1.0/24`, or `{"mode": "subnet", "block": "..."}`.
Returns the network and last addresses, netmask, wildcard mask, first and last usable host, the address and
usable-host counts, and `specialPurpose`: the rows of the IANA IPv4 Special-Purpose Address Space registry
(plus the multicast range 224.0.0.0/4 from the IANA IPv4 Multicast Address Space registry) the block falls
in or overlaps. A /31 counts two usable hosts (RFC 3021) and a /32 one; for /0 to /30 the network and
broadcast addresses are not counted as usable (RFC 1122, section 3.2.1.3).

VLSM: `{"mode": "vlsm", "parent": "...", "requirements": [{"label": "...", "hosts": n}, ...],
"pointToPoint31": false}`. Each request gets the smallest block of at least hosts + 2 addresses (with
`pointToPoint31: true`, a request for exactly 2 hosts gets a /31 instead, RFC 3021); requests are placed
largest block first, each aligned to its own size. A 0-host request is refused (`zeroHosts`); a request no
block of the parent can hold is listed in `unallocated`. The result states `placement`, whether the parent
was typed with host bits set (`parentMasked`), and the free space left as CIDR blocks (`freeBlocks`).

Supernet: `{"mode": "supernet", "prefixes": [...]}` merges the prefixes into the fewest blocks that cover
exactly the same addresses, and gives the single smallest prefix that covers them all, with the addresses it
adds.

Overlap / gap: `{"mode": "overlap", "prefixes": [...], "scope": "..."}` lists every overlapping pair
(identical, contains, contained; two CIDR blocks are either nested or disjoint) and the gaps: inside the
scope when one is given, else between the lowest and highest prefix.

`prefixes` is an array of CIDR strings, or one string of them separated by new lines, commas or spaces
(at most 1,024). Host bits in any block are masked off.

get.description:
Parses the text of a dig answer (BIND 9 dig, the default layout and the +ttlunits, +nottlid and +multiline
variants) into its version line, header, flags and section counts, EDNS OPT pseudo-section, sections and
records, footer, and warning codes. Nothing is resolved.

TTLs are given in seconds. When dig printed a TTL in units (+ttlunits, such as `1h30m` or `1d`) the record
keeps the printed text in `ttlText` and `ttl` is its value in seconds; a record printed without a TTL
(+nottlid) has `ttl: null` and the result carries the warning `ttl-absent`. For a negative answer (NXDOMAIN, or
NOERROR with no answer) with an SOA in AUTHORITY, `negative` gives the negative-caching TTL: the smaller of
the SOA record's TTL and its MINIMUM field (RFC 2308, section 5). Where dig 9.20 prints a placeholder for an
opcode or RCODE that has an IANA name, the header adds it: RESERVED6 is `opcodeName: DSO` and RESERVED11 is
`statusName: DSOTYPENI` (RFC 8490).

Text that is not dig output is not refused: `hadHeader` is false and the sections are empty.

get.description:
One line in: a link IP MTU (68 to 65535) followed by optional tokens. Encapsulations (`gre`, `ipip`, `6in4`,
`vxlan`, `geneve`, `wireguard` or `wg`, `pppoe`, or `+N` for a custom overhead of 1 to 2000 bytes) and MPLS
labels (`mpls`, or `mpls2` to `mpls8`) spend bytes inside the link MTU and shrink the inner IP MTU and the TCP
MSS; 802.1Q tags (`vlan`, `qinq`) sit in the frame header and grow the Ethernet frame instead. `v6` sizes the
IP-carrying encapsulations with an IPv6 outer header.

MPLS labels are counted inside the frame payload (RFC 3032 section 3.1, 4 bytes per label stack entry, section
2.1): `labelTotal` is subtracted from the MTU with `encapTotal`, `shimTotal` counts 802.1Q and QinQ tags only,
and `underlay.requiredMtu` is 1500 + `encapTotal` + `labelTotal` (one label on a 1500-byte packet needs a
1504-byte payload, RFC 3032 section 3). `underlay` is present when the stack has at least one encapsulation or
label.

get.description:
Normalises a MAC address (colon, hyphen, Cisco dot or unseparated; 12 hex digits, 16 for EUI-64) or a bare
OUI (6 hex digits), looks the OUI up in the embedded IEEE MA-L snapshot, and reads the I/G bit (unicast or
multicast) and the U/L bit (universally or locally administered).

`wellKnown` is present when a standard or registry, not the OUI holder, gives the address its meaning: the
IPv4 multicast mapping 01-00-5E-00-00-00 to 01-00-5E-7F-FF-FF with the 32 groups that share the MAC (RFC 1112
section 6.4), the IPv6 multicast mapping 33-33 with the group's low 32 bits (RFC 2464 section 7), the VRRP
virtual router MACs with their VRID (RFC 9568 section 7.3), other named rows of the IANA Ethernet Numbers
registry, and the IEEE standard group addresses (the IEEE 802.1Q reserved block 01-80-C2-00-00-00 to 0F,
which bridges do not relay, and the IS-IS and ES-IS addresses).

The tool does not refuse input with HTTP 400: an input that is not a MAC or an OUI returns HTTP 200 with
`ok: false` and `error.message`.

get.description:
Paste the output of a routing table command and get every route parsed into the same fields, the default routes of each table with the one that wins, and, on request, the route a destination would use. Four printouts are recognised: Linux iproute2 (`ip route`, `ip route show table all`, `ip -6 route`, `ip -d route`), Linux net-tools (`netstat -rn`, `route -n`), BSD and macOS `netstat -rn`, and Windows `route print` (IPv4 and IPv6, Active and Persistent Routes). Field meanings follow ip-route(8), ip-rule(8), rtnetlink(7), route(8), netstat(8), FreeBSD netstat(1), Apple netstat.1 and Microsoft Learn's route pages, read on 2026-10-19.

The request is the printout as text (parse only), or a JSON object `{"text": ..., "lookup": ...}` (parse, then look the address up). The lookup applies RFC 1812 section 5.2.4.3: basic match, then longest match, then the lowest metric among equal lengths. For iproute2 it reads table local, then main, then default (the three default rules of ip-rule(8)); other tables are listed in `skipped`. A winning `throw` route continues in the next table. On Windows only Active Routes are consulted. A route iproute2 prints without a metric is compared as metric 0 (in the capture behind the golden vectors, route -n showed Metric 0 for such a route).

Nothing is dropped: tokens that are not understood stay in the route's `unparsed`, and lines that are neither a route nor known structure are listed in `unparsedLines`. Text that is not a routing table is not refused: `format` is `unknown`.

get.description:
The RFC 6811 section 2 validation state of one route against the VRPs (Validated ROA Payloads) you send:
Valid when at least one VRP matches, Invalid when at least one covers and none matches, NotFound when none covers.
Nothing is fetched: there is no RPKI repository or validator behind the operation, so the answer holds for the
VRPs in the request and no others.

`route` is a prefix and its origin AS, such as `192.0.2.0/24 AS64496` (asplain or asdot, RFC 5396), or `NONE`
for the origin value RFC 6811 defines; an origin of AS 0 is refused (RFC 7607 section 2). `vrps` is text with one
VRP per line (prefix, optional maxLength, AS; `prefix-maxLength` also accepted; `#` starts a comment), or an RFC
8416 SLURM document as text or as a JSON value, whose prefixAssertions are read as the VRPs and whose
prefixFilters are counted, not applied. Without a maxLength a VRP authorises the exact prefix only (RFC 9582
section 4.3.2.2).

Each VRP comes back with `covers` and a `relation`: `match`, `wrong-as`, `too-specific`,
`wrong-as-and-too-specific`, `as0` (an AS 0 VRP never matches, RFC 6811 section 2 and RFC 6483 section 4),
`origin-none`, `not-covering` or `other-family`. `maxLengthNotes` lists every VRP (AS 0 aside) whose maxLength
is longer than its prefix, with the number of prefixes it authorises, the case RFC 9319 section 5 asks
operators to avoid.

parameters.description: The request object as a URL-encoded JSON string.

400.description: A request that is not the { route, vrps } object, a route or VRP that does not parse, a prefix with bits set beyond its length, an origin of AS 0, an AS number beyond four octets, a maxLength outside the prefix length to 32 or 128, a SLURM document with another slurmVersion or an undefined member, or more than 20000 VRPs.

originAs0.summary: A route whose origin is AS 0 is malformed (reject vector route-origin-as0, RFC 7607 section 2)

value.message: a Route with origin AS 0 is malformed and is never validated: RFC 7607 section 2 says a BGP speaker MUST NOT originate or propagate it

get.description:
Classifies where a URL would send a server-side request, from the URL string alone: nothing is resolved and
the request is never issued. The host is read from the raw input, so the inet_aton spellings of an IPv4
address (decimal, octal, hex, short form) are decoded and reported as obfuscation. Every address is matched,
most specific row first, against the IANA IPv4 and IPv6 Special-Purpose Address Space registries (read
2026-10-19), and the row is returned in `specialBlock`; the cloud metadata addresses outrank their covering
row.

An IPv6 address that carries an IPv4 address is rated by the address it carries: IPv4-mapped (::ffff:0:0/96),
the deprecated IPv4-compatible form (::/96, `canonicalIp` in mixed notation), NAT64 under 64:ff9b::/96 or
64:ff9b:1::/48 (RFC 6052 layouts, `embeddingLayout`), 6to4 (2002::/16), and Teredo (2001::/32, RFC 4380
section 4: `teredo` gives the server, the client with the XOR undone, the client port and the flags, and the
more internal of server and client decides). `embeddedIpv4` is the deciding address and
`embeddedSpecialBlock` its IPv4 registry row. `anycastService` is true when the deciding address is a
registry anycast service address (PCP, TURN, DNS-SD SRP, 6a44 relay). Dangerous non-HTTP schemes and
embedded credentials are flagged. `reasons` are explanatory sentences in English.

An empty input is refused with HTTP 400 (`missing_input` when nothing is sent; `invalid_input`, "Enter a URL
or host to classify.", for whitespace only).

decimalMetadata.summary: Decimal-encoded metadata URL, the page's Example (golden vector)

reasons: the host is a decimal encoding of 169.254.169.254 - a common way to hide an internal address from a filter
169.254.169.254 is a cloud instance-metadata endpoint (IMDS)

teredoLoopback.summary: Teredo address whose client carries loopback (golden vector)

reasons: a Teredo address (2001::/32, RFC 4380 section 4): bits 32 to 63 carry the server 8.8.8.8, and the last 32 bits carry the client 127.0.0.1 stored XOR 0xFFFFFFFF (client port 337, stored XOR 0xFFFF)

rated by the client address 127.0.0.1, the more internal of the two: 127.0.0.0/8 is loopback (the host itself); the IANA IPv4 Special-Purpose Address Space registry lists 127.0.0.0/8 as "Loopback" (RFC 1122, Section 3.2.1.3), not globally reachable
RFC 4380 section 4 says global Teredo identifiers "MUST include a global scope unicast IPv4 address"; this one names an internal target, so a filter must reject it

ipv4Compatible.summary: Deprecated IPv4-compatible address carrying loopback (golden vector)

reasons: an IPv4-compatible IPv6 address (::/96, RFC 4291 section 2.5.5.1) carrying 127.0.0.1 in its low 32 bits
127.0.0.0/8 is loopback (the host itself); the IANA IPv4 Special-Purpose Address Space registry lists 127.0.0.0/8 as "Loopback" (RFC 1122, Section 3.2.1.3), not globally reachable

RFC 4291 section 2.5.5.1 says the IPv4-compatible address "is now deprecated" and that the IPv4 address it carries "must be a globally-unique IPv4 unicast address"; a stack that still accepts the format reaches the carried address, so it is rated by it

nat64Loopback.summary: NAT64 Well-Known Prefix carrying loopback (golden vector)

reasons: a NAT64 address under the Well-Known Prefix 64:ff9b::/96 (RFC 6052) carrying 127.0.0.1 in its low 32 bits
127.0.0.0/8 is loopback (the host itself); the IANA IPv4 Special-Purpose Address Space registry lists 127.0.0.0/8 as "Loopback" (RFC 1122, Section 3.2.1.3), not globally reachable

RFC 6052 section 3.1 says the Well-Known Prefix MUST NOT represent non-global IPv4 addresses and translators MUST drop such packets; the address still names that internal target, so a filter must reject it

192.0.0.10 is a special-purpose anycast service address: the TURN anycast address, answered by the topologically nearest TURN server (RFC 8155); the IANA IPv4 Special-Purpose Address Space registry lists 192.0.0.10/32 as "Traversal Using Relays around NAT Anycast" (RFC 8155), globally reachable

specialBlock.name: Traversal Using Relays around NAT Anycast

gopher.summary: Dangerous scheme gopher:// to loopback (golden vector)

reasons: 127.0.0.0/8 is loopback (the host itself); the IANA IPv4 Special-Purpose Address Space registry lists 127.0.0.0/8 as "Loopback" (RFC 1122, Section 3.2.1.3), not globally reachable
the gopher:// scheme is a common SSRF escalation vector (it can reach the local filesystem or internal services)

format.description: The command that printed the text.

interfaces.description: The Windows Interface List (empty for other formats).

mac.description: As printed; empty for the loopback.

defaults.description: The default routes (prefix length 0) of each table or section.

unparsedLines.description: Lines that are neither a route nor known structure, kept as pasted.

structureLines.description: Headers, rulers, section titles and echoed command lines recognised.

line.description: 1-based line number of the route's first line.

raw.description: The route's text; continuation lines joined with a new line.

section.description: iproute2: the table (main when no `table` token is printed); Windows: ipv4-active, ipv4-persistent, ipv6-active, ipv6-persistent; BSD: inet or inet6; net-tools: main.

prefix.description: address/length, or null when the destination is not an address with a length.

type.description: The iproute2 type; reject or blackhole from BSD and net-tools flags; unicast otherwise.

gateway.description: The next hop as printed, or null.

onLink.description: Delivered directly on the interface (no gateway used).

interface.description: dev, Iface, Netif, the Windows Interface address or the IPv6 If number.

metricText.description: The metric as printed when it is not a number (Windows Persistent Routes: Default).

src.description: iproute2 src, the preferred source address.

id.description: RTF_* name (BSD and macOS) or LINUX_* (route(8)); null when no manual lists the letter.

attributes.description: Other documented attributes (pref, mtu, nhid, ...) and extra columns (Refs, Use, Expire, Ref, MSS, Window, irtt), as printed.

consulted.description: Whether a lookup reaches this table or section.

winner.description: The index that wins, or null.

stages.description: The tables or sections consulted, in order.

unusable.description: Same-family routes left out because the destination is not an address with a length.

candidates.description: Basic match: routes whose prefix contains the destination.

survivors.description: Longest match: the candidates of the largest length.

CgnRequest.description: The request of one of the three modes, named by `mode`.

pool.description: A prefix, a range A-B, one address, or a count of addresses (1 to 16,777,216).

blockSize.description: Ports per block, at most the usable ports of one address.

blocksPerSubscriber.description: Blocks one subscriber may hold; default 1.

inside.description: Or the demand as an inside prefix (its host addresses) or range.

logFormat.description: 150-byte or 175-byte per-session messages (RFC 7422 section 1); default nat444.

inside.description: I: a prefix (its host addresses, as RFC 7422 section 2.3 counts a /28 as 14) or a range.

outside.description: O: one address, a prefix (every address) or a range.

reserved.description: R: ports and ranges separated by commas; default 0-1023.

compressionRatio.description: C; default I / O rounded up. C x O must cover I.

dynamicFactor.description: D; default 0 (no dynamic pool beyond the division's remainder).

maxPorts.description: M, the maximum ports per user.

reverse.description: Reverse lookup: an outside address, a port and, optionally, a UTC time.

recordTime.description: The timestamp for the RFC 7422 section 3 configuration record (UTC).

offset.description: a, the PSID offset; RFC 7597's default is 6.

psidLength.description: k, the PSID length; a + k is at most 16.

psid.description: The PSID, 0 to 2^k - 1: a number, or a string in decimal or 0x hexadecimal.

port.description: A port whose PSID is wanted.

first.description: null when the pool was given as a count.

systemPortsExcluded.description: True when the range starts above 1023.

portsPerSubscriber.description: blockSize x blocksPerSubscriber, the per-subscriber limit (RFC 6888 REQ-4).

subscribersPerAddress.description: floor(blocksPerAddress / blocksPerSubscriber): every subscriber's blocks on one address (RFC 6888 REQ-2).

spare.description: poolSubscribers - subscribers; negative when the pool is too small.

log.description: Per-session figures from RFC 7422 section 1, divided by the block size as RFC 7768 section 2 says; computed, not measured.

ranges.description: Split only where a reserved port intervenes.

list.description: R as ranges joined by commas.

systemPortsReserved.description: False when any of 0-1023 is left as a candidate.

dynamicPoolPorts.description: candidatePorts - C x portsPerSubscriber, on each outside address.

overflowPortsPerUser.description: M - portsPerSubscriber when M is larger.

dynamicDisabledButLeftover.description: D = 0 and the division left ports over.

timeInWindow.description: null unless a time and a configuration window are given.

inside.description: The inside address, for a deterministic port.

configRecord.description: The record with its timestamp, when recordTime is given.

excludedLow.description: The A = 0 block, 0 to 2^(16 - a) - 1, when a > 0.

excluded.description: True when A is 0 and a > 0: no CE owns the port.

requiredMinEchoRx.description: Required Min Echo RX Interval; absent or 0 refuses to loop Echo packets.

demand.description: Demand mode requested; active only while the session is Up.

sessionUp.description: false for Down, Init or AdminDown: every Desired Min TX is raised to 1 s.

section.description: The document and section, e.g. RFC 5880 section 6.8.4, or computed: <rule>.

scope.description: Optional: a block whose uncovered space is listed as gaps.

CidrPrefixList.description: Up to 1,024 IPv4 CIDR blocks, as an array or as one string separated by new lines, commas or spaces.

CidrResult.description: Subnet mode: the breakdown of one IPv4 CIDR block and its special-purpose classification. (Before 2026-10-19 the operation returned the nine breakdown fields only; `mode` and `specialPurpose` were added then.)

input.description: The input, trimmed. Host bits are preserved here; see `network` for the masked base address.

broadcast.description: The last address of the block: the directed broadcast for /0 to /30; for a /31 or /32 a host address.

netmask.description: The subnet mask in dotted-decimal form.

wildcard.description: The inverse (wildcard) mask, as used in ACLs.

totalAddresses.description: Total addresses in the block (2 ^ host bits).

usableHosts.description: Addresses assignable to hosts: total - 2 for /0 to /30; 2 for a /31 (RFC 3021); 1 for a /32.

CidrSpecialPurposeClassification.description: The block against the IANA IPv4 Special-Purpose Address Space registry (read 2026-10-19, registry updated 2025-10-09; its two-block NAT64/DNS64 row split in two) plus 224.0.0.0/4 from the IANA IPv4 Multicast Address Space registry: 27 rows. It reports the registry's rows only; it does not check allocation or routing.

status.description: special: the whole block lies in a listed range; partial: the block holds one or more listed ranges and other addresses; none: it meets no listed range.

matches.description: The ranges holding the block (most specific first), then the ranges it contains (in address order).

specialAddresses.description: Addresses of the block inside any listed range, nested rows counted once.

CidrSpecialPurposeMatch.description: One registry row the block meets, as the registry gives it. A null flag is a cell the registry leaves blank or a column it does not have.

terminated.description: Termination Date, YYYY-MM; null where the registry says N/A.

source.description: Source: valid as the source address of a datagram that transits two devices.

destination.description: Destination: valid as its destination address.

forwardable.description: Forwardable: a router may forward it between external interfaces.

globallyReachable.description: Globally Reachable: forwardable beyond a specified administrative domain.

footnote.description: The registry footnote on the row: 1 on Loopback's flags, 2 on 192.0.0.0/24.

registry.description: Which IANA registry the row comes from.

relation.description: equal: the same block; inside: the block lies within the row; contains: the block holds the row and more.

overlapAddresses.description: Addresses the block and the row have in common.

parentMasked.description: True when the typed parent had host bits set and was masked to `parent`.

subnets.description: The allocated blocks, in placement order (largest block first).

unallocated.description: The requests that did not fit, as given.

freeBlocks.description: The free space left in the parent, as the largest aligned CIDR blocks, in address order.

placement.description: How the requests were ordered before placement.

utilizationPct.description: usedAddresses / parentSize x 100, one decimal place.

label.description: The request's label, or an empty string.

broadcast.description: The block's last address (a host, not a broadcast, on a /31).

pointToPoint31.description: True for a /31 given under the pointToPoint31 option (no network, no broadcast).

inputAddresses.description: Addresses in the union of the inputs (overlaps counted once).

aggregated.description: The minimal set of aligned blocks covering exactly the union.

singleSupernet.description: The smallest single prefix covering every input.

supernetExtraAddresses.description: Addresses the single supernet adds beyond the union.

kind.description: a is identical to b, a contains b, or a is contained in b. partial cannot occur between two CIDR blocks and is kept for completeness.

gaps.description: Uncovered space inside the scope, or between the lowest and highest prefix when no scope is given.

coveredAddresses.description: Addresses the prefixes cover (clamped to the scope when one is given).

expanded.description: Eight groups of four hex digits.

prefix.description: Prefix arithmetic, when a prefix length was given.

eui64Mac.description: The MAC inside a modified EUI-64 interface identifier (ff:fe in the middle), else null.

teredo.description: The Teredo fields of a single 2001::/32 address (no prefix, or /128), else null.

type.description: The special-use type, e.g. Global unicast, Documentation, Teredo, Multicast, Source-specific multicast.

scope.description: Multicast or link-local scope name, e.g. global, link-local, "reserved (scope F)", "unassigned (scope 6)".

embeddedIpv4.description: The dotted IPv4 tail of an IPv4-mapped or IPv4-compatible address.

scopeStatus.description: Multicast only: the status of the 4-bit scope value.

flags.description: Multicast only: the flag nibble read bit by bit.

ssmRange.description: Source-specific multicast only: the group-ID range the address falls in.

countExact.description: The exact address count as a decimal string.

Ipv6Teredo.description: RFC 4380 section 4, flags as updated by RFC 5991 section 3.1.

server.description: The Teredo server's IPv4 address (bits 32 to 63).

flags.description: The 16-bit Flags field in hex with C, U and G read out.

port.description: The client's mapped UDP port (bits 80 to 95 XOR 0xffff).

client.description: The client's mapped IPv4 address (bits 96 to 127 XOR 0xffffffff).

ok.description: False when the input is not a MAC or an OUI; then only input and error are present.

hex.description: Normalised hex (6, 12 or 16 digits), upper case.

vendor.description: The IEEE MA-L registrant, or null when none applies (multicast, locally administered, or not in the snapshot).

local.description: The U/L bit: true when locally administered.

isOuiOnly.description: The input was a bare OUI.

OuiWellKnown.description: A meaning set by a standard or registry rather than by the OUI holder.

name.description: The registry's or standard's own name, in English.

vrid.description: VRRP only: the Virtual Router Identifier (the last octet); 0 is reported with a note, outside the 1 to 255 RFC 9568 defines.

ipv4Groups.description: IPv4 multicast only: the 32 groups that map to this MAC.

ipv6Low32.description: IPv6 multicast only: the group address's last 32 bits, as two hex groups.

bridgeFiltered.description: IEEE 802.1Q reserved block only: not relayed by bridges.

mtu.description: The link IP MTU as given.

outer.description: The outer IP version used to size IP-carrying encapsulations.

layers.description: The resolved stack, in the order given.

kind.description: encap and label spend bytes inside the MTU; shim grows the frame.

variable.description: The size is a documented base that options can exceed (GENEVE).

labelTotal.description: MPLS label stack bytes, 4 per entry; 0 without an mpls token.

shimBytes.description: 802.1Q and QinQ bytes in the header.

efficiency.description: Wire efficiency of a full-sized TCP/IPv4 segment, (MTU - 40) / (MTU + 38), in percent.

underlay.description: Present when the stack has an encapsulation or an MPLS label.

requiredFrame.description: The frame that MTU implies, with this stack's tags.

opcode.description: As dig printed it (QUERY, NOTIFY, UPDATE, RESERVED6, ...).

status.description: The RCODE as dig printed it (NOERROR, NXDOMAIN, RESERVED11, ...).

opcodeName.description: The IANA name where dig prints a placeholder: RESERVED6 is DSO (RFC 8490).

statusName.description: The IANA name where dig prints a placeholder: RESERVED11 is DSOTYPENI (RFC 8490).

extra.description: Further OPT lines (COOKIE, NSID, EDE, ...), verbatim.

negative.description: For a negative answer with an SOA in AUTHORITY, the negative-caching TTL (RFC 2308 section 5).

soaTtl.description: The TTL on the SOA line, in seconds.

minimum.description: The SOA's MINIMUM field, in seconds.

hadHeader.description: False when the text is almost certainly not dig output.

ttl.description: In seconds; null for a question and for a record printed without a TTL (+nottlid).

ttlText.description: The TTL as printed, kept only when dig printed it in units (+ttlunits).

class.description: IN, CH, HS, ...; empty when dig printed no class.

rdata.description: The record data on one line (+multiline records joined); empty for a question.

type.description: A, AAAA, MX, NS, CNAME, TXT, PTR, SRV or SOA.

fields.description: MX, SRV and SOA values in labelled fields.

referralNote.description: "Authoritative answers can be found from:" was present.

recognized.description: False when the text is almost certainly not nslookup output.

DigCommandRequest.description: Every field is optional; a name (or `reverse`) is needed for a command.

type.description: A mnemonic from the IANA registry, TYPEnn, ANY, AXFR or IXFR. Default A.

ixfrSerial.description: For IXFR: the client's SOA serial (written ixfr=N).

reverse.description: -x: an IPv4 or IPv6 address; name, type and class are then not needed.

server.description: @server: a host name or an address; empty means the resolvers in /etc/resolv.conf.

port.description: -p; empty means the transport's default (53, 853 for TLS, 443 for HTTPS).

ok.description: False when an error finding stops the build.

command.description: The command on one line; empty when ok is false.

explain.description: The id of the explanation (tools.dig-command-builder.explain.<id> on the page).

findings.description: Errors first, then warnings, then infos.

effective.description: What the query will carry; null when ok is false.

bufsize.description: The advertised size, or null for dig's default.

addresses.description: One or more controller IPv4 addresses, separated by spaces, commas or semicolons.

vendor.description: The vendor profile the value was built from.

subOption.description: The sub-option code, where the vendor defines one.

addressForm.description: binary: four bytes per address; ascii: one address as text; ascii-list: the addresses as one text joined by ", ".

multiple.description: Accepts more than one controller address.

vendorClass.description: The option 60 vendor class the vendor requires.

useOption.description: The option to use instead, for encoding other-option.

access_date.description: The day the page was last read and checked.

unreachable.description: Why it could not be re-read, with the date.

hex.description: The value in lower-case hex, for encoding hex.

text.description: The value as text, for encoding string or other-option.

breakdown.description: How a hex value was built, byte group by byte group.

host.description: The host as written (brackets removed from an IPv6 literal).

isIp.description: The host is, or decodes to, an IP address.

canonicalIp.description: Dotted IPv4, or RFC 5952 IPv6 text (mixed notation for the IPv4-mapped, IPv4-compatible and NAT64 Well-Known Prefix forms).

obfuscated.description: The host was an inet_aton spelling of an IPv4 address other than plain dotted decimal.

reasons.description: Why, in English sentences, quoting the registry row and the RFCs.

schemeFlag.description: A non-HTTP scheme that escalates SSRF.

embedding.description: The IPv4-in-IPv6 layout decoded, if any.

embeddedIpv4.description: The carried IPv4 address that decides the rating (for Teredo, the more internal of server and client).

embeddingLayout.description: The RFC 6052 prefix length whose layout produced embeddedIpv4 (NAT64 only): 96 for 64:ff9b::/96; 48, 56, 64 or 96 for 64:ff9b:1::/48.

specialBlock.description: The IANA special-purpose registry row the address falls in (most specific), or null.

embeddedSpecialBlock.description: The IANA IPv4 registry row of the carried address, for an IPv4-in-IPv6 host, or null.

teredo.description: The decoded Teredo fields, when embedding is teredo; else null.

serverIpv4.description: Bits 32 to 63, the Teredo server, as stored.

clientIpv4.description: Bits 96 to 127 XOR 0xFFFFFFFF: the client's mapped IPv4 address.

clientPort.description: Bits 80 to 95 XOR 0xFFFF: the client's mapped UDP port.

flags.description: Bits 64 to 79, the 16-bit Flags field (RFC 4380, RFC 5991).

anycastService.description: The deciding address is a registry anycast service address (PCP, TURN, DNS-SD SRP, 6a44 relay).

SsrfSpecialBlock.description: One row of the IANA IPv4 or IPv6 Special-Purpose Address Space registry, as IANA writes it.

globallyReachable.description: The Globally Reachable column; null where the registry gives none (192.88.99.0/24, 2001:10::/28, 2001::/32, 2002::/16).
